$Comment:
Extends the jar's own Sawmill.json (RPG Stations) via the SCOPED action target {Station: Sawmill, Action: Mill}: a station is an ordered list of self-contained actions, so an extension names the ACTION it adds to rather than the whole station, and naming the station beside it pins this progression to the jar's own sawmill. That scope is the deliberate choice here: an action id is not globally unique, so a bare {Action: Mill} target would also attach this XP to any other pack's action answering to Mill. The bare form is still the right one when the target is a shared, Ref'd ActionAsset that several stations reuse and the extension is meant to reach all of them. Own-asset references are authored PascalCase, matching the referenced file's own name; matching stays case-insensitive so a casing slip never breaks content.

The jar owns the sawmill's presentation, its custody and its recipe; this extension owns what progression means at it and how the Crafting tree's Sawmill techniques change the one Mill action for the player who holds them.

(1) PerCycleContributions - the sawmill's entire progression path. The jar's Mill action declares no contributions of its own (RPG Stations is completely progression-agnostic by design, its shipped content ships inert, the same pattern as the vanilla Affinity_* assets), so this extension owns the sawmill's progression outright rather than adding a slice on top of an existing jar award. Both entries post to the mmoskilltree:skill_xp channel (Param = skill id), forwarded verbatim on the cycle-completed event and consumed by the MMO bridge, which awards it as skill XP: WOODCUTTING at 8.0/cycle, CRAFTING at 4.0/cycle. That 2:1 split is the ratio every weighted score in the referenced lootables mirrors - the station's own skill counts full, the adjacent one counts half - so re-tuning these two amounts and re-tuning those weights are the same design decision expressed twice, and they should move together. Mill also authors its own ContributionScale (the same tool-quality ladder its Bonus rolls use), which PRE-SCALES these amounts before the cycle-completed event fires, so nothing here needs to apply a multiplier a second time: the amount on the event is always the amount to grant. XP is per cycle, so a Rip Cut cycle (two logs) pays what any cycle pays, and a gathered Lumberyard cycle pays at the idle rate, a tenth (the Mill authors no Work.Idle, so the engine's default fraction applies).

(2) Bonus.Lootables - one concern per table, unioned onto the jar action's own Bonus (Lootables and Rolls both union, so the jar's session-loyalty SawmillFinds table and its tool-ladder rolls all keep firing alongside these): SawmillLuckFinds and SawmillDeepFinds are the find-tier ladder's two bands, and Mmo_Sawmill_Treasure_Luck and Mmo_Sawmill_Treasure_Deep the same two bands one floor higher for a Treasure Cut player; SawmillOutputLadders is the pair of bonus-PLANK ladders, and Mmo_Sawmill_Bulk_Order their second payment for a Bulk Order player; SawmillMasterworkBonus is the single tool-gated roll rewarding a worker who brings the Sawmiller's Hatchet to the bench; Mmo_Sawmill_Talents is what the Crafting tree's station stats pay at this bench, and Mmo_Sawmill_Find_Essence its Essence of Life half; Mmo_Sawmill_Sap_Tap and Mmo_Sawmill_Second_Shift are two Crafting talents read off the talent's own record; Mmo_Sawmill_Quarter_Saw is Quarter Saw's second find roll. Every table a technique changes is opt-in: a Mill Trade table rolls only for the talent's holder, and an everyday table a trade turns off carries a Requires whose Not names the trade, so a server with Crafting switched off (or no Crafting track at all) pays every everyday table exactly as before.

This pack ships a FOURTH table that does not belong in the list above: Lootables/SawmillTrophy.json, the luck-scaled hatchet chase. It carries the id of a table the RPG Stations jar already references from the Sawmill's own Bonus, so folding it by that id replaces the jar's version in place and it runs without being named anywhere here. Listing it would reference one table twice. That is the general rule for an id OVERRIDE: reference a table from an extension only when you are ADDING it, never when you are replacing one the base already pulls in.

(3) The Mill Technique and the Lumberyard, as per-player settings on the one Mill action (never a second action, so a pile loaded by anyone is the same pile for everyone, and a player who changes their talents mid-pile just mills it the new way). Each reads the talent's own record (ziggfreedcommon:track_pick, its rank the count), so a player without the talent, and a server without the Crafting track, reads 0 or nothing and mills exactly as the jar authors:
- Rip Cut: Recipe.Batch runs two conversions a cycle for its holder (Min 1 plus the talent's rank, held at 2), each taking its own log of the species the cycle converts, so a cycle saws two logs into twice the planks (with one log left it saws the one). Tool.Durability.Ladder doubles the hatchet's wear for its holder (floor 10 is the talent itself); Mill Practice takes a quarter of the extra wear off a rank (floors 11 and 12 read the talent at weight 10 plus Mill Practice at weight 1, so 1.75 and 1.5). A fractional wear pays its whole part and the fraction as the chance of one point more.
- Quarter Saw: Pace (an extension's own ladder, multiplying the jar's, which has none) makes each cycle half again as long for its holder, 4805 ms becoming 7208; its second find roll is Mmo_Sawmill_Quarter_Saw, gated on the talent inside that table.
- Lumberyard: Work.Unattended lets the Mill keep sawing a load while nobody is there, for a load placed by a player holding Lumberyard (Requires, asked of the loader as each load is placed and kept on the pile, so a respec later or a sharer topping the pile up never stops it). MaxQuantity is how many logs one load hands to that work, 40 plus 10 a rank of Lumberyard II (50, 60), read of the loader: the pile itself still holds the Mill's 100 for working by hand. GatherMaxCycles is how many sawn cycles one gather pays for, 24 plus 4 a rank of Lumberyard II (28, 32), read of whoever gathers; each settle still runs at most the jar's default 24 at a time. The planks land in the Mill's own pile, and the finds and XP for them pay to whoever gathers, rolled against that player.

The deterministic part of output quantity is NOT re-authored from here: how many planks a cycle yields by default lives end to end in the jar action's own Recipe.Yield plus its Bonus rolls (its tool-ladder Floors and its chance-gated windfall roll), so this extension never re-authors that number. On top of that deterministic amount, a loot Roll may still add a bounded, ADDITIVE bonus via Grants.OutputItems (N extra items of the cycle's own primary output, never a copy of the whole produced stack); SawmillOutputLadders uses exactly that route, and stays directly comparable to (never a multiplier on) the Recipe.Yield number since both are counted in the same units.
